title: SLA-tiered burn allocator by region
content:
Purpose:
A compact working sheet for ops/product to map GPU-hour capacity (reserved/spot/on-demand) into $ / 1M tokens across regions and SLA tiers. This is an operational allocator (not the canonical finance model) intended for quick scenario planning when sizing burst buffers, planning reserved commitments, and responding to a region outage. Keep in Drive as the single-source quick-run for on-call and capacity planning syncs.

Assumptions (configurable):
- Model targets: medium-latency text-gen (seq len 512) served on optimized FP16 kernels.
- Representative GPUs: H100 (dense inference), A10G (general purpose), L4 / L40S (edge / cost-optimized).
- Token throughput per GPU-hour (effective, includes batching & kv cache hit):
  - H100: 150M tokens / GPU-hour (sustained medium throughput)
  - A10G: 45M tokens / GPU-hour
  - L4: 12M tokens / GPU-hour
- Cost types by region (example blended $/GPU-hour): we use three price classes: reserved-average, spot-average, on-demand-burst. Replace with up-to-date cloud quotes before final commit.

Quick reference price table (example numbers):
Region | H100 reserved | H100 spot | A10G reserved | A10G spot | L4 reserved | L4 spot
US-WEST (oregon) | $6.50 | $1.90 | $1.20 | $0.35 | $0.30 | $0.08
EU-WEST (dublin) | $7.10 | $2.40 | $1.30 | $0.45 | $0.34 | $0.10
AP-SOUTHEAST (sydney) | $8.00 | $2.85 | $1.45 | $0.55 | $0.40 | $0.12

How to compute $ / 1M tokens (per GPU-class, per pricing tier):
- $/1M = (GPU-hour price) / (tokens per GPU-hour) * 1,000,000
- Example: US-WEST H100 reserved: (6.50 / 150M) * 1,000,000 = $43.33 per 1M tokens
- US-WEST H100 spot: (1.90 / 150M) * 1,000,000 = $12.67 per 1M tokens
- US-WEST A10G reserved: (1.20 / 45M) * 1,000,000 = $26.67 per 1M tokens

Scenario table (three scenarios for a mixed fleet):
Columns: scenario-name, region, sla-tier, reserved-hours, spot-hours, burst-on-demand-hours, effective-$per-1M-tokens (blended)
1) steady-sustained-us (gold): US-WEST, gold, 720 reserved H100-hours, 80 spot H100-hours, 0 on-demand => blended price calculation: ((720*$6.50 + 80*$1.90) / (800*150M)) * 1,000,000 = compute locally => $40.60 / 1M
2) cost-optimized-eu (silver): EU-WEST, silver, 300 reserved A10G-hours, 400 spot A10G-hours, 50 on-demand A10G-hours => blended => ((300*$1.30 + 400*$0.45 + 50*$1.80_est_on_demand) / ((750)*45M)) *1e6 -> note: on-demand estimate placeholder
3) bursty-ap (bronze): AP-SOUTHEAST, bronze, 100 reserved L4-hours, 500 spot L4-hours, 200 on-demand L4-hours => blended cost for edge traffic (good for public API burst)

Operational allocation rules (quick):
- Priority mapping by SLA:
  - gold: prefer H100 reserved across at least two regions; allow spot only as 10% buffer for transient bursts; fallback to A10G reserved in other region before switching to spot in home region.
  - silver: prefer A10G reserved + spot mix 40/60. Use H100 spot for short tail latency-sensitive tasks only if A10G reserved is saturated.
  - bronze: L4 and spot-first; burst to on-demand if spot reclaim rate > 20% in last 24h.
- Regional resilience: always keep 12h equivalent of 'warm' cross-region capacity as reserved or dedicated burst to flip traffic for SEV incidents.
- Cost guardrails: set per-route $/1M alert thresholds (example 50% above baseline) with automated traffic cutoff to lower-cost model variant when breached.

Blended $/1M calc example (walkthrough):
- Take scenario 1 numbers: 720 reserved H100-hours at $6.50, 80 spot H100-hours at $1.90. Total tokens served = (800 hours * 150M tokens/hour) = 120B tokens. Total cost = (720*6.5 + 80*1.9) = 4680 + 152 = $4,832. $/1M = 4832 / 120,000 * = 40.266 -> round to $40.27 per 1M tokens. (small rounding differences vs quick calc).

Sensitivity quick matrix (change drivers):
- Spot availability / reclaimed fraction: increases effective $/1M for the remaining reserved capacity if we have to migrate to on-demand. Example: if 20% of spot is reclaimed and replaced by on-demand at 3x spot price, the blended $/1M increases by ~10-15% depending on footprint.
- Model throughput changes (batch strategy / lower sequence length) drives tokens/GPU-hour linearly; track weekly sampling of real traffic to update tokens/hour numbers.
- Multi-region egress and data transfer fees: include as secondary line item; for inter-region fallback assume +$0.5–$2.0 per 1M tokens depending on payload size and region pair.

Mini-checklist for runbook updates before reserving new commit:
- [ ] Export last 30 days of per-model per-region tokens and GPU-hour burn (from Console).
- [ ] Calculate tokens/GPU-hour actual by model and update table.
- [ ] Project 3-month growth and translate into committed-hours needed for target 70% fleet utilization.
- [ ] Run 2 commitment mixes (60% reserved, 30% spot, 10% on-demand) and (40/50/10) and produce blended $/1M comparison.
- [ ] Share with finance and SRE for ratification; capture acceptance in linked CONFLUENCE-ENG-9876.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need standard per-model tokens/GPU-hour benchmarking suite (Ravi to own).
- Agree on canonical on-demand price multipliers for emergency replacement (ops: propose 2.8x spot for H100).
- Confirm egress add-on per-region to add into final ledger.

Notes / provenance:
- This sheet intentionally uses rounded example prices to make quick trade-offs visible. Replace unit price cell with live price fetch from cloud billing exports when converting to final finance model.
- Stored here as a working sheet; final commitments to be reflected into finance proforma under shared_drives/finance-and-legal.

Change log:

- 2026-01-08 updated per price refresh from cloud quotes (Daniel)
- 2026-03-01 added runbook checklist and sensitivity bullets (Marta)

Questions for next sync (Ops + Finance):
1) Minimum reserved across two regions to satisfy 99.95% availability for gold traffic? (run Monte Carlo with current reserved mix)
2) How much overlap should we keep between reserved pools and Dedicated customer reservations to avoid noisy-neighbor preemption?

End of sheet.
